item.title: Governed Hybrid Agency: A Critical Evidence Map of Cognitive Architectures for Foundation-Model Agents
item.description: Background. Cognitive architectures specify the persistent memories, representations, learning processes, and control loops that allow an artificial agent to remain coherent across tasks and time. Foundation models provide broad generative competence, but do not by themselves ensure grounded action, reliable long-horizon memory, calibrated uncertainty, execution monitoring, or accountable learning. item.description: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) continues to be the primary tool in pharmaceutical, environmental, food, and bioanalytical laboratories; however, creating a reliable method is still a gradual, repetitive, and skill-dependent process. item.description: Abstract Large language models have extended software-development assistance from token-level completion to systems that can navigate repositories, edit files, execute tools, and iterate on test feedback. item.description: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. item.title: What makes an LLM a tutor? A component-centric survey of LLM-based and agentic tutoring systems
item.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are reshaping intelligent tutoring systems (ITSs) by reducing authoring costs and enabling flexible interaction. However, effective tutoring requires more than fluent responses. It also depends on pedagogical control, domain grounding, learner modeling, interaction design, orchestration, and reliable evaluation. item.title: When to Delegate: A Measurement Study of Bounded Agent Teams for Personal Super Agents
item.description: Abstract Personal super agents coordinate many tools while remaining fast, safe, and accountable to one user. A popular design is a Router delegating to Workers. item.title: Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Theory-Aligned Social Science Content Analysis: Evidence From Collaborative Learning Discourse
item.description: Theory-based content analysis is central to social science research, but coding context-dependent interactional discourse remains difficult to scale. This study examines whether fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support theory-aligned, episode-level coding of complex social interaction, using socially shared metacognitive regulation (SSMR) in collaborative learning discourse as a demanding empirical case. item.title: Delegating or Doing? Understanding User Behavior in Hybrid Human–Agent Interfaces
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into applications, allowing users to complete tasks either through direct manipulation or by delegating actions to conversational agents. However, little is known about how users balance these modalities when both are available. item.title: Personas shift clinical action thresholds in large language models
item.description: Clinical large language model (LLM) deployment is shifting from feasibility to liability, while current guidance largely treats model behavior as a control problem. item.description: Despite algorithm-level innovations for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), the underlying infrastructure for large-scale MARL remains underexplored. Existing training frameworks primarily optimize for single-agent scenarios and fail to capture the graph-structured nature of MARL. item.description: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) protect private memory and attest initial code and configuration, but neither constrain nor attest shared channels between TEEs or with the untrusted host. item.description: LLM agents increasingly rely on tool calling to complete tasks. Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes tool calling between LLM agents and tool providers.
